monuments.name: Eiffel Tower
monuments.note: Built as the entrance arch of the 1889 World's Fair and meant to last twenty years; it was the tallest structure on Earth until 1930.

monuments.name: Arc de Triomphe
monuments.note: Napoleon ordered it after Austerlitz in 1806; it took thirty years, and twelve avenues radiate from the star around it.

monuments.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
monuments.note: A granite islet crowned by a Benedictine abbey, in a bay where the tide is said to come in as fast as a galloping horse.

monuments.name: Colosseum
monuments.note: Opened in AD 80 with a hundred days of games; some 50,000 spectators sat under a canvas awning worked by sailors.

monuments.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
monuments.note: It began to lean in 1178, while it was still being built on soft ground; engineers took 40 cm off the lean between 1990 and 2001.

monuments.name: St Peter's Basilica
monuments.note: Michelangelo designed the dome of the largest church in the world, raised over the traditional tomb of Saint Peter.

monuments.name: Sagrada Familia
monuments.note: Gaudí gave it the last 43 years of his life and is buried in its crypt; begun in 1882, it is still being built.

monuments.name: Alhambra
monuments.note: The palace-fortress of the Nasrid sultans of Granada, its courts lined with carved stucco and cooled by water from the Sierra Nevada.

monuments.name: Guggenheim Bilbao
monuments.note: Frank Gehry's titanium-clad museum on the Nervión, whose success gave a name to the 'Bilbao effect'.

monuments.name: Elizabeth Tower
monuments.note: Big Ben is strictly the 13.7-tonne bell inside; the tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee.

monuments.name: Tower Bridge
monuments.note: A bascule bridge dressed as a Gothic castle; its two leaves still rise to let tall ships into the Pool of London.

monuments.name: Stonehenge
monuments.note: Raised in stages from about 3000 BC; its axis lines up with the midsummer sunrise and the midwinter sunset.

monuments.name: Brandenburg Gate
monuments.note: Berlin's neoclassical gate, crowned by the Quadriga, stood in the no man's land of the Wall until 1989.

monuments.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
monuments.note: Ludwig II's fairy-tale castle, still unfinished when he died in 1886; it inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

monuments.name: Atomium
monuments.note: Built for the 1958 World's Fair: an iron crystal cell magnified 165 billion times, its spheres joined by tubes and escalators.

monuments.name: Kinderdijk Windmills
monuments.note: Nineteen windmills built around 1740 to keep the polders of the Alblasserwaard drained, and most of them still turn.

monuments.name: Charles Bridge
monuments.note: Prague's stone bridge over the Vltava, begun under Charles IV in 1357 and lined with thirty Baroque statues.

monuments.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
monuments.note: Ivan the Terrible built it on Red Square to mark the capture of Kazan; each of its chapels wears its own dome.

monuments.name: Parthenon
monuments.note: The temple of Athena on the Acropolis, finished in 438 BC; its columns swell and lean so that they look straight.

monuments.name: Hagia Sophia
monuments.note: For nearly a thousand years the largest cathedral in the world; its dome seems to float on a ring of forty windows.

monuments.name: The Little Mermaid
monuments.note: Edvard Eriksen's bronze of Hans Christian Andersen's mermaid, only 1.25 metres tall, on a rock in Copenhagen harbour.

monuments.name: Hallgrímskirkja
monuments.note: Reykjavík's concrete church, its stepped tower modelled on the basalt columns that lava forms as it cools.

monuments.name: Borgund Stave Church
monuments.note: A wooden stave church from about 1180, its tiered roofs watched over by carved dragon heads.

monuments.name: Gergeti Trinity Church
monuments.note: A 14th-century church alone on a ridge at 2,170 metres, under the glaciers of Mount Kazbek.

monuments.name: The Registan
monuments.note: Samarkand's great square, framed by three madrasas covered in blue tilework: the heart of the Timurid city.

monuments.name: Persepolis
monuments.note: The ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid kings, founded by Darius I around 518 BC and burned by Alexander in 330 BC.

monuments.name: Baalbek
monuments.note: Roman temples of Jupiter and Bacchus, raised on foundation stones that weigh up to 800 tonnes each.

monuments.name: Ziggurat of Ur
monuments.note: A stepped temple mound built around 2100 BC for Nanna, the moon god of the Sumerian city of Ur.

monuments.name: Taj Mahal
monuments.note: The white marble tomb Shah Jahan built for Mumtaz Mahal; its stone shifts from pink to white to gold with the light.

monuments.name: Sigiriya
monuments.note: A palace on top of a rock 180 metres high, entered between the paws of a colossal stone lion, built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century.

monuments.name: Golden Temple
monuments.note: The holiest gurdwara of Sikhism, its gilded sanctum standing in a pool; its kitchen feeds tens of thousands every day.

monuments.name: Great Wall of China
monuments.note: Not one wall but many, built and rebuilt over two thousand years; its surveyed branches add up to 21,196 km.

monuments.name: Forbidden City
monuments.note: The palace of the Ming and Qing emperors for five centuries: 980 buildings behind a moat and a ten-metre wall.

monuments.name: Terracotta Army
monuments.note: Some 8,000 life-size clay soldiers buried with China's first emperor around 210 BC, no two faces alike.

monuments.name: Potala Palace
monuments.note: The winter palace of the Dalai Lamas, thirteen storeys climbing the Red Hill above Lhasa at 3,700 metres.

monuments.name: Bagan
monuments.note: More than 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas still stand on the plain, of over 10,000 built between the 11th and 13th centuries.

monuments.name: Angkor Wat
monuments.note: The largest religious monument on Earth, built for Vishnu in the early 12th century; its five towers are lotus buds.

monuments.name: Petra
monuments.note: The Nabataeans carved their city into rose-red sandstone; the Treasury's façade is cut straight out of the cliff.

monuments.name: Burj Khalifa
monuments.note: The tallest building in the world since 2010, 828 metres to the tip of a spire visible from 95 km away.

monuments.name: Tokyo Tower
monuments.note: Modelled on the Eiffel Tower and 13 metres taller, painted white and international orange for air safety.

monuments.name: Mount Fuji
monuments.note: Japan's highest peak, a near-perfect cone of a volcano that last erupted in 1707.

monuments.name: Himeji Castle
monuments.note: The White Heron, Japan's finest surviving feudal castle, which came through the bombing of 1945 almost untouched.

monuments.name: Petronas Towers
monuments.note: The tallest twin towers in the world, joined by a skybridge at the 41st floor; each plan is an eight-pointed star.

monuments.name: Marina Bay Sands
monuments.note: Three hotel towers carrying a 340-metre SkyPark, with an infinity pool nearly 200 metres above the bay.

monuments.name: Borobudur
monuments.note: The largest Buddhist temple in the world, a 9th-century mountain of terraces holding 504 statues of the Buddha.

monuments.name: Taipei 101
monuments.note: Once the tallest building in the world, it rides out typhoons on a 660-tonne steel ball hung near its top.

monuments.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
monuments.note: The main palace of the Joseon kings, founded in 1395, burned in the invasions of 1592 and rebuilt in 1867.

monuments.name: Mount Everest
monuments.note: The highest point on Earth, 8,849 metres; Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary first stood on it in 1953.

monuments.name: Genghis Khan Equestrian Statue
monuments.note: A 40-metre steel horseman on the steppe east of Ulaanbaatar; you can walk out onto the horse's head.

monuments.name: Hassan II Mosque
monuments.note: Built partly over the Atlantic in Casablanca, with a 210-metre minaret and a roof that slides open.

monuments.name: Pyramids of Giza
monuments.note: The Great Pyramid of Khufu was the tallest thing people had built for almost 4,000 years, the last ancient wonder still standing.

monuments.name: Great Sphinx
monuments.note: A lion with a king's head, carved from the bedrock of the Giza plateau around 2500 BC, facing the sunrise.

monuments.name: Abu Simbel
monuments.note: Ramesses II's temples, cut into a cliff above the Nile; in the 1960s they were sawn apart and lifted 65 metres, out of Lake Nasser's way.

monuments.name: Great Mosque of Djenne
monuments.note: The largest mud-brick building in the world; every year the whole town replasters it at the Crépissage festival.

monuments.name: Elmina Castle
monuments.note: Built by the Portuguese in 1482, the oldest European building south of the Sahara, later a hub of the Atlantic slave trade.

monuments.name: Rock-Hewn Churches of Lalibela
monuments.note: Eleven medieval churches carved downward into the living rock, joined by trenches and tunnels.

monuments.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
monuments.note: Africa's highest mountain, a free-standing volcano of three cones whose summit glaciers are shrinking fast.

monuments.name: Victoria Falls
monuments.note: Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders': the Zambezi falls more than 100 metres along a curtain 1.7 km wide.

monuments.name: Avenue of the Baobabs
monuments.note: A dirt road lined with Grandidier's baobabs up to 800 years old, the last of a forest long since cleared.

monuments.name: Table Mountain
monuments.note: A flat-topped sandstone massif over Cape Town, often draped in the cloud the city calls its tablecloth.

monuments.name: Statue of Liberty
monuments.note: A gift from France in 1886: copper skin on an iron frame designed by Gustave Eiffel, turned green within a few decades.

monuments.name: Empire State Building
monuments.note: Built in 410 days during the Depression, it was the tallest building in the world for almost forty years.

monuments.name: Golden Gate Bridge
monuments.note: The longest suspension span in the world when it opened in 1937, painted a colour called International Orange.

monuments.name: Mount Rushmore
monuments.note: Four presidents, each face 18 metres tall, carved into the granite of the Black Hills between 1927 and 1941.

monuments.name: Space Needle
monuments.note: Built in 400 days for the 1962 World's Fair in Seattle, on a foundation deep enough to ride out earthquakes.

monuments.name: CN Tower
monuments.note: Toronto's communications tower, the tallest free-standing structure in the world from 1976 until 2007.

monuments.name: Niagara Falls
monuments.note: Three falls on the border of Canada and the United States, together the most powerful waterfall in North America.

monuments.name: Château Frontenac
monuments.note: A railway hotel built as a château on the cliff above Quebec City, said to be the most photographed hotel in the world.

monuments.name: Citadelle Laferrière
monuments.note: The largest fortress in the Americas, built by Henri Christophe after Haiti's independence to hold off a French return.

monuments.name: The Pitons
monuments.note: Two volcanic spires rising straight out of the Caribbean on the south-west coast of Saint Lucia.

monuments.name: Chichen Itza
monuments.note: At the equinoxes the afternoon sun draws a serpent of light down the northern stairs of El Castillo.

monuments.name: Teotihuacan
monuments.note: A city of perhaps 100,000 people around AD 450, laid out along the Avenue of the Dead below the Pyramid of the Sun.

monuments.name: Christ the Redeemer
monuments.note: An Art Deco statue of reinforced concrete and soapstone on the 700-metre peak of Corcovado, arms open over Rio.

monuments.name: Angel Falls
monuments.note: The highest uninterrupted waterfall in the world, 979 metres off the lip of the tepui Auyán-tepui.

monuments.name: Las Lajas Sanctuary
monuments.note: A neo-Gothic basilica built across a river gorge in the south of Colombia, a few kilometres from Ecuador.

monuments.name: Machu Picchu
monuments.note: An Inca estate built around 1450 on a ridge above the Urubamba, missed by the Spanish and made famous in 1911.

monuments.name: Moai of Rapa Nui
monuments.note: Nearly a thousand stone figures carved by the Rapa Nui; most stand with their backs to the sea, watching over the villages.

monuments.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
monuments.note: One of the few glaciers on Earth that is not retreating; its 70-metre front calves into Lago Argentino.

monuments.name: Sydney Opera House
monuments.note: Jørn Utzon's shells took sixteen years to build, and their roofs carry more than a million glazed tiles.

monuments.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
monuments.note: The 'Coathanger', opened in 1932, its steel arch rising 134 metres above the harbour.

monuments.name: Uluru
monuments.note: A sandstone monolith sacred to the Anangu, rising 348 metres from the desert and glowing red at sunset.

monuments.name: Moeraki Boulders
monuments.note: Spherical concretions up to two metres across, weathered out of the mudstone cliffs of the Otago coast.

monuments.name: Nan Madol
monuments.note: Nearly a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt columns off Pohnpei, the seat of the Saudeleur dynasty.

monuments.name: Mount Yasur
monuments.note: One of the most accessible active volcanoes in the world, erupting several times an hour for at least 800 years.

monuments.name: The South Pole
monuments.note: The bottom of the world, on ice 2,700 metres thick; Amundsen's party reached it first, on 14 December 1911.
